_about: Ground truth for podcast-two-voices.mp3 (espeak-ng, two voices, 0.4s gaps): each line's start and end in ms.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Okay, we're recording. Welcome back to Loose Ends.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: I'm here with Maya Okafor, who just finished her first headline tour.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Hi, thanks for having me. Sorry I was late, the traffic was awful.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: No worries. Did you get a coffee? There's some in the kitchen.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: I'm fine, I've had three already today.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Fair enough. So, before the tour, I want to go back to the very beginning.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Tell me about your first ever gig, because I've heard it did not go to plan.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Oh no. Okay. So I'm nineteen, I've booked a slot at a pub in Leeds, and I've told everyone I know.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: I walk on stage, I plug in my guitar, and the whole pub's power goes out. Every light, the fridges, everything.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: No way. What did you do?

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The landlord's shouting, people are using their phone torches, and I just thought, well, I'm here now.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: So I unplugged, stood on a chair in the middle of the room and played the whole set acoustic in the dark.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: And honestly it's still the best gig I've ever played. Forty people singing along by torchlight. I've been chasing that feeling ever since.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: That's incredible. That's a film scene.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Quick note for listeners: this episode is out on Thursday, and the video is on our channel.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: If you want to support the show there's a link in the description.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Do you want me to mention the merch?

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Go for it. Anyway. Let's talk about the new single.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: A lot of artists listening want to know how you plan a release. What's your approach?

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The biggest mistake I made early on was announcing a song the same week it came out. Nobody had time to care.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Now I start eight weeks out. I tease a fifteen second clip, I let people ask what it is, and I don't answer yet.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Four weeks out I open the pre-save and show the cover. Two weeks out I play it live and film the crowd.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: By release day, people feel like they've been part of it. That's the whole trick, make them feel involved before it exists.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: So it's less about the song and more about the story around it.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The song has to be good. But a good song nobody's waiting for just disappears.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: That's such useful advice.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Okay, we're nearly out of time. Where can people find you?

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: I'm Maya Okafor everywhere. The single's out on the twentieth.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Amazing. Thanks for coming in.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Thanks for having me.
